skills.trigger: When evaluating a retrocardiac cystic lesion with an air-fluid level on chest imaging to distinguish pulmonary sequestration from other cystic or infectious etiologies.
steps: Identify the presence of a retrocardiac cystic mass containing an air-fluid level, which indicates communication with the tracheobronchial tree or superinfection.
Assess the adjacent lung parenchyma for compensatory emphysema or hyperinflation, suggesting a congenital malformation rather than simple acquired infection.
Search for a dilated systemic feeding artery (often arising from the descending aorta) or a prominent/dilated azygos vein indicating anomalous systemic venous drainage.

Differentiate from bronchogenic cysts (typically fluid-filled without air-fluid levels unless infected and lacking systemic vessels), lung abscesses (usually lack compensatory hyperinflation and specific systemic vascular anomalies), and pneumonia (solid consolidation rather than cystic structure).
